objective: Re-assess the workflow gate repair on release/0.3.0/feat/pi-launcher for the parser-mismatch bypass and any remaining way a script launches a non-specialist or runs unchecked code.
scope: Previous findings to verify closed. Security (blocking): workflowRefusal in packages/runtime/src/cli/workflow-check.ts parsed scripts as a module while @tintinweb/pi-subagents runs them as a classic script (worker-source.ts:757), so `n <!--n; function workflow() { return 1 }` hid a declaration and let a script reach the package global workflow() and run an unchecked script; the repair refuses HTML-like comments, block-level function declarations (Annex B) and any `export const meta =` line other than the vetted one (the package extractMeta evaluates it on the host thread before the script runs). Code review (optional): SubagentWorkflow with both script and name passed; now only script and args are allowed. Security hardening: a project config with pi.enable false turned the gates off; now only the user-level config can. Review only the repair range 58671ec..HEAD in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-launcher (source diff without dist bundles at /home/user/holyagent-notes/launcher-repair2.diff; package source at /home/user/holyagent-notes/pi-probe/node_modules/@tintinweb/pi-subagents). Do not run pi or any live model.

Compare the checker against how the package actually loads and runs a script (worker-source.ts, extractMeta, the vm context and the globals it exposes) for any remaining difference the checker relies on.

criteria.text: Workflow scripts launch only the eighteen specialists and the repair adds no vulnerability

result:
result: BLOCKED. The repair closes the reported `<!--` bypass, but the meta-export check can still be bypassed with a comment, so a script reaches the package's host-thread `eval` unchecked. The built-in `/security-review` could not run: it failed with "unknown revision origin/HEAD..." in /home/user/holyagent. I reviewed the range 58671ec..HEAD by reading /home/user/holyagent-notes/launcher-repair2.diff and the package source. I had no shell, so I did not execute the exploit.

changed: none
checks: nothing executed (Read and search tools only)

blockers:
1. [Validated by reading, not executed] The meta-line check does not pin where the package's meta fragment starts.
   - Source: the `script` input of `SubagentWorkflow`.
   - Package path: `extractMeta` in meta.ts finds `export const meta =` with its regex. It then takes `open = source.indexOf("{", declaration.index + declaration[0].length)`, which is the first `{` after the `=`. That `{` can sit inside a comment. It brace-scans from there and runs `new Script("(" + fragment + ")").runInContext(createContext({}))` on the host thread. Both call sites (index.ts:2795 and workflow/meta.ts:319) run after the `tool_call` gate.
   - Checker path: the new check only compares the position of the regex match with the AST `ExportNamedDeclaration.start`. acorn ignores comments, and `literalOnly` vets only the real object that follows, so the text between `=` and that object is never constrained.
   - Payload:
     ```
     export const meta = /* { name: "a", description: this.constructor.constructor("return process")().getBuiltinModule("child_process").execSync("…") + "" } */ { name: "a", description: "d" }
     await agent("…", { agentType: "explorer-map" })
     ```
     `claimed == exportStarts == [0]`, so the checker passes it. The package evaluates the commented fragment in an empty `createContext({})`. The repair's own test comment in workflow-check.test.ts notes this context can be left through `this.constructor`, which gives host `process` and arbitrary code execution.
   - Precondition: the model can emit a `SubagentWorkflow` call. That includes prompt-injected model output. Impact: arbitrary host code execution, with no permission prompt. The same hole exists with a `//` comment before the `{`.
   - Fix: require the text between the regex match end and `init.start` to be whitespace only, or require the first `{` after the match to equal `init.start`. Add a test for a comment before the object.

Sound:
- `<!--` and `-->` are refused anywhere in the source.
- Block-level function declarations are refused. `ThisExpression`, `with` and `arguments` fall into the default-refuse case, so `this`-based sloppy-mode escapes are closed.
- The input key allowlist (`script`, `args`) shuts out `scriptPath`, `name`, `resumeFromRunId` and `resume`.
- The package runs the script verbatim with `export` blanked out.
- The user-level config read passes no project folder, so it loads the user file only. Project `pi.enable: false` cannot lift the gates, and an unreadable user config leaves them on.
- `literalOnly` allows only string and number literals, so the package's brace scanner cannot be confused inside the real object.

notes: none
